newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease on political uncertainty.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.12 percent on slim turnover on Monday and traders said the market was likely to remain in a holding pattern until the formation of a new government following general elections in November.
"I do not see a bright future for our market soon," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.
The 10-share SBI index fell 1.35 points to 1,158.7, almost unchanged from a week ago but off some 5.2 percent from its pre-election level.
Turnover fell to 66.8 million tolars from 110.5 million. Overall seven shares fell, six rose and one remained unchanged, while another 11 were untraded.

Three weeks after Slovenia's general election on November 10, it remains unclear who will form the government as parties on the left and right, which won an even number of seats in the 90-member parliament, insist on their own candidates for prime minister.
Cerar said uncertainty over the effects of the planned introduction of a new tax on trading profits next year was adding to investors' worries.
Drug producer Lek's issue A, which debuted on the Ljubljana bourse in September, was the most actively traded share. It firmed 1.34 percent to 18,850 tolars on volume of 1,911 shares.
Bank SKB, which last month said it plans an issue of global depository receipts early next year, led the day's decliners. The stock fell 2.26 percent to 41,040 tolars on volume of 123 shares.
Prefered shares of bank Hipotekarna bank Brezice topped the day's gainers, firming 3.00 percent to 3,500 tolars on volume of 200 shares.
